newsitem.title: USA: UPS, Nippon Cargo in marketing pact.
newsitem.headline: UPS, Nippon Cargo in marketing pact.

text.p: United Parcel Service (UPS) and Nippon Cargo Airlines said on Friday the companies reached a long-term marketing and operating strategic agreement.
The agreement is the first between two major all-cargo airlines, the companies said in a joint statement.
UPS and Nippon Cargo, the only specialized all-cargo carrier in Japan, will work together to offer service to the international shipping public.
The first phase of the agreement is effective October 30, 1996, the companies said.

In the second phase, the carriers, subject to government approvals, plan to establish a code-share service in the summer of 1997, when UPS expects to introduce B747-200 jet freighter aircraft to serve the Los Angeles market nonstop.
The code-share services between UPS and Nippon Cargo will be the first operated by a U.S. carrier and a Japanese carrier, the companies said.
The agreement is the result of the successful conclusion of a U.S.-Japan all-cargo aviation agreement in April of this year, the companies said.
